title: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
seo_title: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance Class 12 Physics Worksheet (NCERT Ch 2)
standard_code: Class 12 Physics, Chapter 2: Electrostatic Potential and Capacitance
standard_text: Electric potential, potential difference, electric potential due to a point charge, a dipole and system of charges; equipotential surfaces, electrical potential energy of a system of two point charges and of electric dipole in an electrostatic field. Conductors and insulators, free charges and bound charges inside a conductor. Dielectrics and electric polarization, capacitors and capacitance, combination of capacitors in series and in parallel, capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with and without dielectric medium between the plates, energy stored in a capacitor.

body_html:
How to think about it

Electric potential V = kq/r is the work done per unit charge in bringing a charge from infinity; W = qV. Two charges have potential energy kq₁q₂/r. Equipotential surfaces are perpendicular to field lines, and no work is done along them.

A capacitor stores charge Q = CV. A parallel plate capacitor has C = ε₀A/d, multiplied by K with a dielectric. In parallel C = C₁ + C₂; in series 1/C = 1/C₁ + 1/C₂. The stored energy is ½CV² = Q²/2C.

Example

2 μF and 3 μF in series?

6 ÷ 5

Answer: 1.2 μF

Example

10 μF at 100 V. Energy?

½ × 10⁻⁵ × 10⁴

Answer: 0.05 J

Common mistakes

  • Adding series capacitors directly.
  • Using kq/r² for potential.
  • Forgetting the ½ in ½CV².
